A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 2SSP research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original pruning experiments across four LLM families, including perplexity, downstream accuracy, runtime measurements, ablations, and qualitative generation examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations, including the appendix results, and reports revised numerical results for part of the Llama-2 ablation.

M1.justification: Both versions retain L2-based FFN neuron selection, corresponding row/column removal, iterative perplexity-based Attention removal, and the same sparsity-balancing equation with alpha = 1.5. The new appendix documents an existing ablation without establishing a change to 2SSP.

E1.justification: WikiText2, C4, FineWeb-Edu, the six downstream tasks, and the qualitative generation prompts are retained. Three-shot evaluation and the sparsity sweep up to 70% already appeared in v1; their greater prominence in v2 does not expand coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain ShortGPT, Sliding Window, BlockPruner, EvoPress, and SliceGPT, alongside the dense reference. Updated publication citations do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Reported model configurations, dataset processing and sample counts, calibration allocations, sparsity settings, metrics, and zero-shot/three-shot procedures remain unchanged. No protocol revision is stated to explain the changed ablation values.

E4.justification: The existing comparison of s1 alone against s1+s2 has revised Llama-2 results in v2 Table 5, reducing the reported benefit of combining stages, especially at 50% sparsity. The qualitative conclusion remains favorable to both stages; the other ablations, sensitivity studies, and generation examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify random seed 0 and average inference timing over 10 runs. Figure 7 retains the same shaded bands, with no added explanation of their statistical meaning or new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: From v1 Table 4 to v2 Table 5, Llama-2 s1-only perplexities at 37.5% and 50% change from 19.69 and 109.19 to 19.94 and 41.73. Its s1+s2 row changes from 9.25/14.64/31.40 to 9.19/18.16/32.85. These are localized ablation revisions; the main benchmark scores, runtime results, figures, and qualitative outputs are unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix A explicitly defines separate input/output importance scores and selection masks for the inverted-pruning ablation through Eqs. (6)–(9), whereas v1 described that control only verbally. The main mathematical formulation, Eqs. (1)–(5), is unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims about combining width and depth pruning, balancing their sparsities, outperforming the selected baselines, and achieving a favorable pruning-time tradeoff are retained. The introduction's added mention of sparsities up to 70% summarizes evidence already present in v1 Figure 3.

C2.justification: Section 3 adds an explicit argument connecting performance to preserving complete information paths through the gate, up, and down projections, contrasting this with magnitude-only pruning. Existing sparsity boundaries and the discussion of factual degradation in generated text remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix A documents how the existing inverted ablation scores input/output dimensions, selects separate top-K masks, and indexes the weight matrices. Hardware, model repositories, dataset preparation, calibration sizes, and code-access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hoang et al. (2023), Revisiting Pruning at Initialization Through the Lens of Ramanujan Graph, to support the information-path rationale. The broader positioning is stable; several other bibliography changes update publication information for existing works.

P1.justification: v2 makes local language corrections, expands the method explanation, moves the few-shot discussion from Appendix A.2 into Section 4.1, and inserts a new technical appendix. The main section sequence remains intact, and the generic Impact Statement is removed.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a two-column conference layout to a single-column journal layout, with extensive resizing and repositioning of tables and figures and revised headers and typography. The former appendix few-shot table becomes main-text Table 3. All ten figures retain their underlying visual content.

improvement.justification: Appendix A improves documentation of the inverted-pruning control. However, v2 Table 5's revised Llama-2 s1+s2 values disagree with the unchanged Table 1 values under the stated settings; these rows agreed in v1. Neither changed settings nor a correction rationale is supplied. The documentation benefit and newly introduced reporting inconsistency leave the net quality change uncertain.
